# The trapezoid fitter's endpoint defect

One seed (0), 5 buckets, `output_partition="quantile"`. This file exists so stage 4's claim rests on regenerable numbers.

## 1. `TrapezoidMembership.evaluate` at its own endpoints

`TrapezoidMembership(a=0, b=0.25, c=0.75, d=1)`:

| x | -0.01 | 0 | 0.1 | 0.5 | 0.9 | 1 | 1.01 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| membership | 0.000 | 0.000 | 0.400 | 1.000 | 0.400 | 0.000 | 0.000 |

Membership at `x == a` is **0.000** and at `x == d` is **0.000**. Correct for an open trapezoid; a defect once a fitter sets `a = data.min()`.

## 2. Mass sitting exactly at each feature's minimum

Unit-scaled inner-train fold — the rows the memberships are fitted from.

| feature | column min | fraction of rows at the min (train) | (test) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Cement | 0.000 | 0.005 | 0.000 |
| Slag | 0.000 | 0.472 | 0.447 |
| FlyAsh | 0.000 | 0.552 | 0.539 |
| Water | 0.000 | 0.006 | 0.000 |
| Superplasticizer | 0.000 | 0.379 | 0.345 |
| CoarseAgg | 0.000 | 0.003 | 0.000 |
| FineAgg | 0.000 | 0.029 | 0.024 |
| Age | 0.000 | 0.134 | 0.155 |

The three worst columns are `FlyAsh` (0.552), `Slag` (0.472), `Superplasticizer` (0.379). If they were independent, 0.853 of rows would be at the minimum of at least one of them — and under the `min` t-norm each of those rows is zeroed for **every** rule. The measured uncovered fraction below is the same order; the difference is that these columns are correlated.

## 3. Uncovered test rows, against bin count and padding

`uncovered` is the fraction of test rows where no rule fires at all — those are answered with exactly 0, which is finite and so survives every NaN filter in the pipeline.

| n_bins | pad=0 | pad=0.05 | pad=0.25 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0.791 | 0.000 | 0.000 |
| 3 | 0.791 | 0.000 | 0.000 |
| 12 | 0.791 | 0.000 | 0.000 |
| 50 | 0.791 | 0.000 | 0.000 |

The `pad=0` column is constant in the bin count — the left edge tracks `data.min()` however many bins there are, which is why coarsening the histogram cannot fix this. Any nonzero pad removes it.
